claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars like Toyota Camry (2018–present) and Toyota RAV4.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a generic metal gearbox/transmission-like housing with shafts/bolts and stamped markings, but no readable Toyota part number, label, or clear identification that it is an oil pump balance shaft assembly for those models.

risks.risk: Wrong part type/model fit (photos look like a gearbox/transmission assembly, not clearly an oil pump balance shaft assembly).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the exact part label/part number/serial plate (or stamped code) and a close-up showing the oil pump/balance shaft features if present.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used transmission/gearbox-type assembly with unknown compatibility (worst-case fit risk).

risks.risk: Missing internal components or incomplete assembly (photos don’t confirm completeness).
risks.proof: A photo/video showing the full unit from multiple angles including all ports/holes, plus confirmation that all internal parts are present (no missing gears/bearings/shafts).

risks.risk: Wear/damage not visible in the provided angles (shaft play, bearing wear, gear tooth wear, cracks).
risks.proof: A clip showing manual rotation of shafts/bearings (smoothness, no grinding), and close-ups of any wear points/cracks around the housing and bearing seats.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working (worst-case condition).

risks.risk: Leakage/contamination (oil/grease residue visible; could indicate leaks or prior failure).
risks.proof: A close-up of the suspected leak areas plus a wipe-clean test showing whether fresh oil appears after cleaning (or a photo of the unit after cleaning).

risks.risk: Condition uncertainty due to lack of testing (no evidence it was operational).
risks.proof: Proof of testing: a short video of the part being run/tested (or a receipt/statement with verifiable test result).

proof_requests: Send clear photos of any label/part number/serial plate (front, side, and any stamped codes) so the exact Toyota application can be verified.
Send close-ups that specifically show oil pump and balance shaft features (not just a gearbox-like housing).
Provide a video rotating the shafts/bearings by hand to show smooth movement and no grinding/play.
Show all sides of the housing and any ports/holes to confirm completeness (no missing internal parts).
Provide evidence of leak status: clean the unit and show whether oil reappears from the same spots.
response.reason: The witness can identify it only as a gearbox/transmission-like engine part assembly, with no reliable proof of the seller’s specific Toyota oil pump balance shaft claim. I can still price it at the worst-case as an unverified, untested, compatibility-unknown used transmission-type assembly.
